#### ! Scenario

*Or what to do when a dependency brings in versions you didn't expect*
This scenario demonstrates the fundamental concept of transitive dependency resolution.

It shows how Maven automatically discovers and includes the dependencies of your direct dependencies, forming a dependency graph.

This is the "happy path" where no conflicts exist.

::: {.callout-note title="Tool Versions"}
This scenario was tested with **Maven 3.9**; the behaviour shown applies to Maven 3.x.
:::

#### ! Example

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 4.4
graph LR
    Root(Project Root) --> LibA(lib-a:1.0.0)
    LibA --> LibB(lib-b:1.0.0)
    LibB --> LibC(lib-c:1.0.0)
```

```{.xml include="pom.xml" snippet="s1-deps"}
```

#### ! Expect
Declaring `lib-a` automatically includes its transitive dependencies `lib-b` and `lib-c` on the classpath.

#### ! Why
Maven reads `lib-a`'s POM, finds `lib-b`, reads `lib-b`'s POM, finds `lib-c`, and collects every unique node it visits. With no version conflicts anywhere in the graph, resolution is a straightforward walk and the result mirrors the declared structure.

#### ! Fix
No fix is needed here. This is the desired behaviour.

#### ! Risk
* LOW A short chain of libraries you control.
* MEDIUM A chain that reaches into third-party frameworks: every one of their transitives is now yours too.
* HIGH Assuming the chain is short. Run the tree before you reason about it.

#### ! Control
Run `mvn dependency:tree` on a new project before adding anything else, and keep the output in mind as the baseline you compare against later.

#### ! Check

```bash
mvn dependency:tree
```

**What to look for:**
A clean tree with no unexpected versions; with `-Dverbose`, no `omitted for conflict` lines.

**Conclusion:**
The dependency graph is healthy and resolving as expected.

#### ! Scales
In large systems, this simple chain `A -> B -> C` is repeated thousands of times, creating a complex web. The "happy path" becomes rare as diamond dependencies emerge.

#### ! Takeaway
One declaration can pull in a whole chain. Transitive resolution is what lets you build on top of giants without naming every library yourself.

#### ! Wild
A fresh Spring Boot web project declares one starter, `spring-boot-starter-web`, and resolves dozens of jars. Nobody on the team chose Jackson, Tomcat or Micrometer; the starter's POM did. That is transitive resolution working exactly as designed, and it is also why "we don't use library X" is a claim you should check with `dependency:tree` rather than with the POM.
